title: A ‘Deep Blue-Kasparov moment for mathematics’
speaker: Tristan Buckmaster
venue: Harvard CMSA · AI for the Working Mathematician
description: I discuss my work with Levent Alpöge on finite-time blow-up for the incompressible Euler equations, the role AI played in the proof, and what that experience suggests about how mathematicians might work with these tools.

title: Computer-Assisted Proofs in Fluid PDEs
speaker: Tristan Buckmaster
venue: London Mathematical Society · General Meeting, Edinburgh
description: A numerical simulation can suggest the shape of a fluid singularity. How can we prove that shape exists? I explain how interval arithmetic puts rigorous bounds on numerical errors, and how those bounds enter a proof of self-similar blow-up.

title: The Shock Development Problem
speaker: Tristan Buckmaster
venue: Institute for Advanced Study · Seminar in Analysis and Geometry
description: What happens just after a shock forms? In joint work with Theodore Drivas, Steve Shkoller, and Vlad Vicol, I follow the shock front and the weaker discontinuities that emerge alongside it in two-dimensional compressible Euler flow with azimuthal symmetry.

title: Stable shock wave formation for the compressible Euler equations
speaker: Tristan Buckmaster
venue: Fields Institute · Workshop on Euler and Navier–Stokes Equations
description: How does a shock first form in a smooth compressible fluid? I describe joint work with Steve Shkoller and Vlad Vicol on how the velocity gradient becomes singular and why shock formation persists under small changes to the initial flow.

title: A rigorous derivation of the kinetic wave equation
speaker: Tristan Buckmaster
venue: Institute for Advanced Study · Analysis and Mathematical Physics Seminar
description: Starting from the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with random initial phases, how does energy move among Fourier modes? I describe joint work with Pierre Germain, Zaher Hani, and Jalal Shatah that uses analysis and number theory to recover the first stages of this transfer.
